channel.title: 100 Doors to Recursion
channel.description: 100 doors into the things I've made with AI, from my first app to the system I run now.

item.title: Door 45: I ask what the task left behind: a skill you run after a task that lists real follow-ups and reports nothing when nothing genuine came up
item.description: whatdidimiss: a skill you run after a task. It lists real follow-ups and reports nothing when nothing genuine came up. Something to try: Clone LucasCooperBey/claude-skills, copy skills/whatdidimiss into ~/.claude/skills, then run it after a task.

item.title: Door 44: I ask how my app could be misused before someone else finds out: a skill that traces risks through the actual code, with file and line evidence
item.description: threat-model: traces risks through your actual code with file and line evidence. It documents risks and does not certify an app secure. Adapted from OpenAI's security-threat-model skill, Apache-2.0 licensed. Something to try: Clone LucasCooperBey/claude-skills, copy skills/threat-model into ~/.claude/skills, then point it at a repository you want modeled.

item.title: Door 43: I like hearing what people remember from a song: a spoken check-in that asks what stuck and compares it with the song brief
item.description: banger-recall: a spoken check-in that asks what stuck from a song and compares it with the song brief. Live scoring needs an API key; sample replays run without one. Something to try: Clone LucasCooperBey/banger-recall and run a sample replay with no API key. Live scoring needs an API key.

item.title: Door 42: I set spending limits on my AI tools: list each paid tool, check its cap, and write down what actually happens when you hit the limit
item.description: spending-limit-checklist: a written checklist. List each paid tool, check its cap, and write down what actually happens when you hit the limit. Something to try: Open the gift file and walk through the list for each paid AI tool: the cap, the alert, and what happens at the limit.

item.title: Door 41: I pick the app worth finishing next: list every project, mark what actually works, and choose one useful next step
item.description: list-every-app: a 15-minute written exercise. List every project, mark each works, broken or unknown, and choose one useful next step. Something to try: List every project, mark each works, broken or unknown, pick one, and finish the sentence: To be useful to one person today, it needs ___.

item.title: Door 40: I want PDFs that print cleanly: reusable patterns for page breaks, images and print layouts
item.description: pdf-generation: a Claude Code skill with reusable patterns for page breaks, images and print layouts in Typst or HTML, with validation and troubleshooting notes. Something to try: Copy the pdf-generation skill into ~/.claude/skills, then use it when a table or image is running off the page.

item.title: Door 39: I hold my page up to the design: compare a screenshot with its reference and get specific fixes
item.description: visual-verdict: a Claude Code skill that compares a screenshot with its reference image and lists specific fixes. Something to try: Copy the visual-verdict skill into ~/.claude/skills, then give it a screenshot and its reference image.

item.title: Door 37: I check what's crowding my AI chat: estimate the space tools and instructions take
item.description: context-budget: a Claude Code skill that estimates the tokens your skills, agents, MCP tools, rules and hooks load, so you can see what to switch off. Something to try: Copy the context-budget skill into ~/.claude/skills, then ask Claude Code to use it to audit your setup.

item.title: Door 36: I like to keep the notes my AI forgets: save working notes to a file your session can read back
item.description: scratchpad: a Claude Code skill that saves working notes to a file when you ask, so a later session can read them back. Something to try: Copy the scratchpad skill into ~/.claude/skills, then type /scratchpad and the note you want saved.

item.title: Door 35: I check my prompts against facts: match a prompt's claims to your real files, then rewrite it
item.description: prompt-grounding: a Claude Code skill that checks a prompt's claims against your actual project files, then rewrites the ask. Something to try: Copy the prompt-grounding skill into ~/.claude/skills, save the prompt as prompt.txt in your project, and ask Claude Code to use the skill on it.

item.title: Door 34: I look for a tool before I build one: find existing solutions and compare their fit first
item.description: deep-recon: a Claude Code skill that searches for existing solutions and compares how well each one fits before you build. Something to try: Copy the deep-recon skill into ~/.claude/skills, then type /deep-recon and the problem in one line, with one search round per agent.

item.title: Door 33: I check a claim before I share it: separate what the sources support from what they don't
item.description: adversarial-research: a Claude Code skill that sends separate verifier agents after each claim and sorts what the sources support from what they don't. Something to try: Copy the adversarial-research skill into ~/.claude/skills, then ask Claude Code to use it on a draft and extract the claims first.

item.title: Door 32: I look for duplicates in my AI setup: a ranked list of overlaps and conflicts
item.description: ecosystem-audit: a Claude Code skill that reviews your .claude setup and returns a ranked list of overlaps and conflicts, and deletes nothing. Something to try: Copy the ecosystem-audit skill into ~/.claude/skills, then ask Claude Code to use it and run the inventory first.

item.title: Door 31: I like listening to my agent's replies: hear an action-first summary instead of reading it all
item.description: earshot: turns the last agent reply into a short spoken summary, action first, using Ollama and a local model on your machine. Something to try: After a long agent reply, run earshot, or type /. in Claude Code, and listen for the action first.

item.title: Door 30: Block risky commands before an AI runs them: safety checks for Claude Code, with limits
item.description: harness-guard: eight Claude Code hooks that refuse risky agent turns, including destructive commands, force pushes to main, secrets leaving the machine, and edits that weaken your linter. Something to try: Run ./install.sh, merge the hooks block from settings.example.json into ~/.claude/settings.json, and restart Claude Code.

item.title: Door 29: Make an AI draft sound like you: check the facts and cut wording you would not say
item.description: writing-check: one Python file that lists the phrases that make a draft read as machine-written, each with its line and the rule behind it. Something to try: Run python3 writing_check.py draft.md on a draft you are about to post.

item.title: Door 28: Review with another model family: a second family asks differently
item.description: review-gate's cross-family mode: a reviewer from the other model family checks each push, and a REJECT blocks it. Something to try: Install the pre-push hook, set REVIEW_GATE_AUTHOR to the family that wrote the code (claude or codex), and push.

item.title: Door 27: Close every chat with a reason: twelve open chats became two
item.description: closeout: one Python file that sorts your recent Claude Code chats into close, keep and merge, and writes a closing note for each. Something to try: Run python3 closeout.py list to see which recent chats are safe to close; it writes nothing until you run sweep.

item.title: Door 26: Turn a long YouTube video into a shorter listen
item.description: yt-condense: give it a YouTube link and it hands back the video as spoken prose at about a fifth of the length, with or without captions. Something to try: Run yt-condense on one long video from your watch-later list and listen to what comes back.

item.title: Door 25: Get the slides from any recorded talk: what was shown and what was said, slide by slide
item.description: talk-to-slides: turns a talk recording into slide images, the text on each slide, and a short HTML report. Something to try: Run talk-to-slides run recording.mp4 --out talk-out on a recording you have the right to process.

item.title: Door 23: Find the right AI tool fast: a hand-reviewed directory with honest pros and cons
item.description: directoryofagents.com, the hand-reviewed directory itself, and the card behind every listing: three rules, a made-up filled example and a zero-code prompt. Something to try: Before you pay for an AI tool, fill in one card for it after an hour of your own use.

item.title: Door 22: Explain anything to anyone: one plain sentence first, the deep detail last
item.description: The breakdown skill: one plain sentence first, then sections at 100,000, 50,000, 30,000 and 10,000 feet, each readable on its own. Something to try: Drop the folder into your Claude Code skills and say "break it down".

item.title: Door 21: Remember why you decided: one dated note per decision
item.description: wiki-write, a Claude Code skill that files one dated note per real decision and keeps an index a later reader searches, plus the by-hand template with a made-up example. Something to try: After any big choice, write one dated file: what you picked, what you passed on, and the reason.

item.title: Door 20: Precompact Protector: keep your place through a compaction
item.description: precompact-protector: two Claude Code hooks that save the last 40 turns before compaction and hand back your last request and the files in play after. Something to try: Merge settings-snippet.json into ~/.claude/settings.json with the real path; nothing to install.

item.title: Door 19: Field Audit: grade your AI setup with receipts
item.description: Field Audit: one paste-in prompt that has Claude Code audit the AI system on your machine, scoring 12 parts with a receipt each and naming every gap. Something to try: Paste the prompt file into Claude Code at your system root; post your scorecard as an issue to join the ledger.

item.title: Door 18: The Spine Pattern: memory that never erases
item.description: The Spine Pattern: 13 principles, a 6-part checklist and a standard-library engine for an append-only log with provenance, typed edges and supersede. Something to try: Run the README's ledger story on a fresh clone: three values kept, two SUPERSEDES edges, nothing erased.

item.title: Door 17: Blind Council: five models argue, one settles
item.description: Blind Council: five models answer on their own, cross-examine each other as MEMBER-A to E, and a sixth model that never debated settles it. Something to try: bun install, put an OpenRouter key in .env, then bun run council "your question" (about one to two dollars for a six-seat run).

item.title: Door 16: CorpusSync: search what you already know
item.description: CorpusSync: ingest notes, documents and YouTube captions into a local Qdrant store, search by meaning and by exact word behind a relevance gate, and get answers from a local Ollama model with numbered sources. Something to try: pip install -e . in a venv, ollama pull nomic-embed-text, then corpussync ingest ./notes --corpus notes and corpussync search.

item.title: Door 15: Changelog Digest: your changelog becomes content
item.description: changelog-digest again (the Door 8 tool): a Python script that reads a markdown changelog and writes a hook, a short story and video ideas. Something to try: Run python3 changelog_digest.py examples/sample-changelog.md --date 2026-03-14 --dry-run to see the prompt without an API key.

item.title: Door 14: ShipGate: no leaked keys go public
item.description: ShipGate: one shell script, ship-gate.sh, that runs gitleaks and trufflehog over the full history and checks the LICENSE, a raw .env and attribution, with one exit code. Something to try: brew install gitleaks trufflehog, put ship-gate.sh on your PATH and run it in a repo before it goes public.

item.title: Door 13: Review gate: fresh eyes on every push
item.description: review-gate: one Python file (standard library only), an install script that writes a pre-push hook, and 45 tests. Something to try: Run install.sh inside your project to add the pre-push hook; it needs the Claude Code CLI signed in and Python 3.10 or newer.

item.title: Door 12: Hooks over reminders: checks on every agent edit
item.description: harness-guard: four quality hooks plus the safety hooks for Claude Code, each a short shell script you can read first. Something to try: Clone it and run ./install.sh, or merge just the four quality-hook lines from settings.example.json into ~/.claude/settings.json.

item.title: Door 11: TabMap: why 200 tabs are open
item.description: TabMap: captures your open tabs, labels each by intent, project, stale or solved, then offers a cleanup that lists before it closes anything. Something to try: Clone it, pip install -r requirements.txt, run python3 -m tab_intel.capture, then preview the cleanup with auto_cleaner.py --dry-run.

item.title: Door 10: Ecosystem MCP: research npm packages from inside Claude Code
item.description: The repo: research, compare and security-check npm packages from inside Claude Code. Something to try: Add it to Claude Code and ask it to compare two packages before you install either.

item.title: Door 9: block-destructive: a Claude Code hook that stops destructive shell commands before the agent runs them
item.description: The hook: refuses rm -rf on root or home, force-pushes to main, git push --no-verify and curl piped into sh; a seatbelt for accidents, not a sandbox. Something to try: Copy block-destructive.sh to ~/.claude/hooks and add it as a PreToolUse hook on Bash.

item.title: Door 8: The changelog that becomes content
item.description: changelog-digest: turn a day of changelog entries into a hook, a short story and video ideas. Something to try: Run the dry run on the sample changelog, then on your own.

item.title: Door 7: The perfection pass: ask for two critique passes before you look
item.description: pp2p and pp3p, two Claude Code skills: two or three critique passes, then a polish. Something to try: Before you read your agent's next piece of work, ask it for two critique passes that try to break it, then a polish.

item.title: Door 6: My Claude Code config, and the ramp: a 53-second first session in May, then 146 sessions from November 8 to December 11
item.description: claude-config-public: the operating-rules template. Something to try: Copy it to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and fill in the 5 placeholders.

item.title: Door 5: treehouse: a git worktree pool for running several coding agents side by side
item.description: treehouse, one bash file that needs only git: spin a worktree per agent, glance at which are dirty on one screen, and sweep only the clean, merged ones. Something to try: Run treehouse spin 3, then treehouse glance.

item.title: Door 4: FriendForm: a form friends fill out from a link
item.description: friendform, the self-hosted form builder: start from a blank form or one of seven templates, share a link, collect and export the answers. Something to try: Run bun install, bun run setup and bun run dev, rebuild one questionnaire you send around as a document, and cut every question you would not act on.

item.title: Door 3: My CRM, started on Replit from two pasted documents
item.description: dataguard, pulled out of that CRM: checks a PostgreSQL or SQLite database for orphaned records, dates out of order, wrong totals and null gaps, with an HTML report. Something to try: Pick one table in a database you own and count the rows that point at a record that no longer exists.

item.title: Door 2: WebPerformanceToolkit: my first app in git, and its 33 hours of simulated scores
item.description: The first prompt template: twelve sections plus the real-data line. Something to try: Before your next build, fill in at least sections 1, 4, 5 and 6, then paste the whole thing as your first message.

item.title: Door 1: RobotTales: bedtime stories where robot siblings teach if/else, loops and variables
item.description: A bedtime-story prompt that teaches one coding idea. Something to try: Paste it into any chat model, fill in the three brackets, and read what comes back before you read it aloud.
